biography: Robert van den Berg, a Dutchman born and bred for speed, first tasted the thrill of racing not on asphalt, but on the frozen canals of his hometown. As a boy, he'd modify his ice skates, pushing the boundaries of what was possible on the slippery surface. This early obsession translated into a passion for karting, quickly dominating local circuits with a raw, aggressive style that both thrilled and terrified his competitors. He ascended through the junior ranks, eventually landing a seat with the Verde Lares team, known for nurturing young talent. While flashes of brilliance hinted at a future champion, inconsistent performances and a tendency to crack under pressure have plagued his career. Now, at 35, van den Berg finds himself fighting to stay relevant, a veteran clinging to the hope of one last shot at glory. He's currently racing in the European Touring Car Championship, hoping to prove he still has what it takes.
drivingStyle: Van den Berg's driving style is a reflection of his personality: aggressive and uncompromising. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and daring overtakes, often pushing his car and tires to their absolute limits. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also makes him prone to errors and tire degradation. He struggles with tire management, often sacrificing long-term pace for short bursts of speed. In high-pressure situations, he tends to become erratic, either pulling off miraculous drives or crashing out spectacularly.
rivalries: Enzo Bellini: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident in their junior karting days, where van den Berg allegedly forced Bellini off the track, costing him the championship.

Anya Petrova: A fierce competitor known for her cool and calculated driving style, Petrova often clashes with van den Berg's aggressive approach, leading to numerous on-track battles and heated exchanges in the media.
Jean-Pierre Dubois: Dubois and van den Berg were teammates for a short period and their rivalry ignited when Dubois felt van den Berg showed him a lack of respect.
quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, even though they are visibly worn and frayed.
Listens to classical music before every race to calm his nerves, a stark contrast to his aggressive driving style.
Refuses to have his car washed during a race weekend, believing it washes away his luck.
famousQuote: "You either go all in, or you go home. There's no point in half-measures in this sport."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2015, after a nail-biting final stint where he held off a charging Enzo Bellini by a mere tenth of a second.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2018 European Touring Car Championship finale, handing the title to Anya Petrova.
